correctness.rationale: For 0<alpha<beta<=4 and finite equality-invariant S, if f_alpha is injective on S then both proportional maps permute S, giving S=(beta/alpha)S, impossible for a nonzero finite set; hence two distinct complementary points are forced by f_alpha(u)-f_alpha(v)=alpha(u-v)(1-u-v). Equality-invariance and S != {0} supply an interior point z, whose separately finite forward orbits satisfy two preperiodicity equations within N iterates. Removing endpoint factors z and (1-z) yields Q_{m,n}; specialization alpha=2 and nonzero leading-beta coefficient show each resultant is a nonzero bivariate polynomial. Summing degree bounds yields B_N candidate z roots and B_N partner values per z; countable union of proper algebraic loci proves null/meagre parameter-pair exceptional set and countable vertical sections. Independent Sympy checked all nine nonzero resultants for N=2, plus exact witness alpha=3/2, beta=3, S={1/3,2/3}. The all-N nonzero proof is analytic, not inferred from the finite check.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a motivated global structural question: despite explicit finite toss-and-catch sets, nearly every pair of distinct logistic parameters has no nontrivial finite equality-invariant set. Constructive algebraic certificates for each size and finite fibers of fixed-alpha partner values give a useful exact rarity obstruction, rather than a tiny-instance type check.

limitations: Only distinct positive-amplitude logistic maps on [0,1] and equality invariance; mere forward invariance differs.
